sentences.text: Parvodus is an extinct genus of hybodont sharks that lived during the Mesozoic era. These animals belong to the class Chondrichthyes, which includes all cartilaginous fishes.
The genus is classified within the family Lonchidiidae.
The genus Parvodus was named by Rees and Underwood in 2001.
There are 81 recorded fossil occurrences of Parvodus in the Paleobiology Database.
The species P. rugianus was described by Ansorge in 1990 from Berriasian-Valanginian deposits in England, Germany, Denmark, and Sweden.
The species P. curvidens was described by Duffin and Thies in 1997 from Kimmeridgian deposits in Germany.
The species P. pattersoni was described by Duffin in 1985 from Bathonian deposits in England and Scotland.
The species P. ominechonensis was described by Breeden et al. in 2024 from Carnian deposits in Japan.
The species P. graciliani was described by Ribeiro and França in 2026 from Tithonian deposits in Brazil. It was named to honor the Brazilian writer Graciliano Ramos.
A 2023 paper assigned the species P. huizodus, from the Early Triassic of China, to the genus Parvodus.
The species P. celsucuspus was reported from the Early Cretaceous of England and France.
A single tooth of Parvodus sp. has been reported from the Upper Cretaceous (Campanian) of France.
The species P. graciliani is known from isolated teeth found in lacustrine deposits of the Aliança Formation in the Jatobá Basin.
The type species of the genus Parvodus is Lissodus rugianus. This species was originally described by Ansorge in 1990.
It is debated whether the species P. heterodon belongs in the genus Parvodus or should be placed in the genus Polyacrodus.
It is debated whether the species "Hybodus" parvidens belongs in the genus Parvodus or should be assigned to the genus Polyacrodus.
